database_summary: This is a traffic/collision reporting database (SQLite) containing one table of collisions (one row per reported collision), a victims table (one row per victim/party involved in a collision), a parties table (one row per party/vehicle/actor in a collision) and a case_ids table that maps case_id to db_year. The collisions table holds mostly descriptive attributes of each collision and some aggregated counts (killed_victims, injured_victims, party_count, broken-out injury counts). The victims and parties tables hold person/party-level observations (injury, role, safety equipment, vehicle attributes, at-fault flag). case_ids is a small mapping table for year partitioning. Joins between collisions and victims/parties are on case_id (and party_number when joining to a specific party/victim). Joining parties to victims may multiply or filter rows depending on party_number availability.

accepted.name: collisions_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  jurisdiction,
  officer_id,
  reporting_district,
  chp_shift,
  population,
  county_city_location,
  county_location,
  beat_type,
  chp_beat_type,
  beat_number,
  primary_road,
  secondary_road,
  distance,
  direction,
  intersection,
  weather_1,
  weather_2,
  state_highway_indicator,
  state_route,
  postmile,
  location_type,
  side_of_highway,
  tow_away,
  collision_severity,
  killed_victims,
  injured_victims,
  party_count,
  primary_collision_factor,
  pcf_violation_code,
  type_of_collision,
  motor_vehicle_involved_with,
  road_surface,
  road_condition_1,
  lighting,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  collision_date,
  collision_time,
  process_date,
  -- derived: numeric sortable timestamp (NULL if date missing)
  CASE
    WHEN collision_date IS NOT NULL
    THEN (replace(substr(collision_date,1,4),'','') || replace(substr(collision_date,6,2),'','') || replace(substr(collision_date,9,2),'','') || coalesce(replace(substr(collision_time,1,2),':',''),'00') || coalesce(replace(substr(collision_time,4,2),':',''),'00') || '00')
    ELSE NULL
  END AS collision_timestamp
FROM collisions
accepted.description: Normalized projection of collisions with key identifying columns and commonly-used measures exposed. Use this as the canonical collisions row for joins or downstream aggregations. Keeps original column names and exposes a derived numeric 'collision_timestamp' (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS numeric) for easy ordering. | Use for: list collisions with location/time and basic measures; join collisions to parties or victims by case_id; order collisions by time or compute time-based trends

accepted.name: victims_by_case_party
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  victim_role,
  victim_sex,
  victim_age,
  victim_degree_of_injury,
  victim_seating_position,
  victim_safety_equipment_1,
  victim_safety_equipment_2,
  victim_ejected
FROM victims
accepted.description: Normalized victims projection one row per victims.id with pass-through case_id and party_number preserved. Useful for person-level analyses, injury counts, safety equipment analyses, and joining back to collisions or parties by case_id and party_number. | Use for: count victims by injury severity or sex; join victims to collisions to allocate injured/killed counts; analyze safety equipment usage among victims

Use for actor-level summaries or joining to collisions/victims. | Use for: identify at-fault parties and their attributes; aggregate party-level injuries or cellphone use; join parties to collisions to analyze vehicle-related factors

accepted.name: collisions_with_party_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS party_row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT v.id) AS victim_row_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.victim_degree_of_injury IS NOT NULL AND trim(lower(v.victim_degree_of_injury)) IN ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victim_killed_count_derived,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.victim_degree_of_injury IS NOT NULL AND trim(lower(v.victim_degree_of_injury)) NOT IN ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal','no injury') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victim_injured_count_derived
FROM collisions c
LEFT JOIN parties p ON c.case_id = p.case_id
LEFT JOIN victims v ON c.case_id = v.case_id
GROUP BY c.case_id
accepted.description: Aggregated counts of parties and victims per collision (case_id). Useful to validate or supplement collisions.party_count and collisions.*_victim counts. Produces one row per case_id with counts of parties, victims, injured victims (by victim_degree_of_injury) and killed victims if recorded in victims. | Use for: compare reported collision-level counts to person-level records; filter collisions by presence/absence of victims or killed victims; quality checks on data completeness across tables

accepted.name: collisions_party_victim_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  c.jurisdiction,
  c.county_location,
  c.primary_road,
  c.collision_date,
  c.collision_time,
  p.id AS party_id,
  p.party_number,
  p.party_type,
  p.at_fault,
  p.party_sex,
  p.party_age,
  p.vehicle_make,
  v.id AS victim_id,
  v.victim_role,
  v.victim_sex,
  v.victim_age,
  v.victim_degree_of_injury,
  v.victim_safety_equipment_1
FROM collisions c
LEFT JOIN parties p ON c.case_id = p.case_id
LEFT JOIN victims v ON c.case_id = v.case_id AND (p.party_number IS NOT NULL AND v.party_number = p.party_number)
accepted.description: Denormalized join of collisions to parties and victims. Keeps collisions.* and preserves parties.case_id, parties.party_number, parties.id (as party_id) and victims.id (as victim_id) so downstream logic can disambiguate rows. One row per combination of collision x party x victim where party_number matches victims.party_number when available; also retains unmatched parties/victims via LEFT JOIN pattern. | Use for: attribute-level inquiries linking victim injuries to party/vehicle attributes; summaries of collisions by road with per-person details; identify mismatches between parties and victims by party_number

accepted.name: case_year_map
accepted.description: Mapping of case_id to db_year from case_ids table. Use to filter or group collisions/parties/victims by ingestion or source year. | Use for: limit analyses to a specific db_year; join year metadata to collisions for time-trend analysis

accepted.name: collisions_rank_by_time
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  cb.case_id,
  cb.collision_timestamp,
  cim.db_year,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cim.db_year ORDER BY cb.collision_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_per_year
FROM collisions_basic cb
LEFT JOIN case_ids cim ON cb.case_id = cim.case_id
accepted.description: Ranks collisions within each db_year (from case_ids) by collision_timestamp descending so callers can select top-N most recent collisions per year by filtering on rank. Exposes collision_timestamp and rank_per_year. Does not apply a fixed LIMIT. | Use for: get the most recent collisions per year (filter WHERE rank_per_year <= K); time-based sampling of collisions for manual inspection
